item.title: CapitaLand India Trust launches CapitaLand Data Centre Chennai 01: 34 MW IT, 53 MW gross, about US$203 million, completion by end 2026
item.description: On 15 October 2026 CapitaLand India Trust (CLINT) launched CapitaLand Data Centre Chennai 01 in Ambattur, Chennai, its first data center in Tamil Nadu, with Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. The facility represents about INR 19.4 billion (US$203.2 million) of investment, will have 53 MW of gross power capacity and 34 MW of IT capacity across 13 data halls when completed by the end of 2026, and is designed for high-density computing including liquid cooling. It is jointly held by CLINT and CapitaLand India Data Centre Fund. CLINT's Navi Mumbai data center is fully leased to a global hyperscaler; no tenant is named for Chennai. Country conversion: another sponsor-built, near-complete shell in India's second data center corridor, launched at head-of-state level. [Signal 60, Corroborated, via The Business Times 15 Oct 2026; The Hindu BusinessLine 15 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: AEP plans about $4 billion for a 702 MW Bloom fuel cell plant near Cheyenne, Wyoming under a 20-year Google PPA
item.description: On 14 October 2026 American Electric Power (Nasdaq: AEP) said it plans to invest about $4 billion in a new 702 MW fuel cell generation project near Cheyenne, Wyoming, selling the output to Google under a 20-year power purchase agreement. The project company, Cheyenne Fuel Cell, LLC, is about 92% owned and controlled by AEP and nearly 8% by funds advised by Basalt Infrastructure Partners. The plant uses Bloom Energy fuel cells, generates power without combustion of natural gas, and includes plans to integrate carbon capture. Construction is planned to start in 2026, with full operation expected by the end of 2028. AEP says the plant supports Google's growing energy needs in the greater Cheyenne area and follows the Google and Black Hills Corp. agreements effective 30 September (already on the Wire). Country conversion: a named hyperscaler now has a second, utility-financed firm generation source for its Wyoming load, built outside AEP's traditional service territory. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via AEP / PR Newswire 14 Oct 2026 (primary)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Fermi discloses a binding 15-year, $6.5 billion TensorWave lease for 222 MW at Project Matador, Texas, backed by AMD credit support
item.description: On 14 October 2026 Fermi Inc. (Nasdaq/LSE: FRMI) furnished an 8-K fact sheet describing a binding 15-year phase one lease with TensorWave at Project Matador in Carson County, Texas: 222 MW of total power capacity including 156 MW of critical IT capacity, $6.5 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term, two 5-year renewal options and 2.5% annual escalators. Fermi develops, builds and delivers turnkey; TensorWave takes occupancy in phases from Q4 2027, completing in early 2028. Fermi cites power capex of $3M to $4M per MW of total power capacity and turnkey data center capex of $10M to $12M per MW of critical IT, and an estimated phase one project-level NOI margin of about 75% to 80% (non-GAAP). AMD signed credit support on 13 October; per the filing it begins only after construction is complete and rent starts on the final delivery phase, and it ends early if TensorWave or its guarantor holds an investment-grade rating for 12 consecutive months. Project financing is not yet closed. Country conversion: the first named, priced tenant lease on a behind-the-meter Texas Panhandle AI campus, with a chipmaker balance sheet behind it. [Signal 78, Confirmed, via Fermi 8-K (Item 7.01, Exhibit 99.1 TensorWave fact sheet) 14 Oct 2026; Fermi x AMD credit support release (Access Newswire) 13 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: PJM files an executed study agreement at FERC to evaluate SB Energy's 10.37 GW Flagship AI campus in Pike County, Ohio under Ohio's State Agreement Approach
item.description: On 13 October 2026 PJM Interconnection filed an executed Study Agreement (FERC Docket ER27-126-000, Rate Schedule No. 54, signed 25 September) with SB Energy affiliates SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect and Portsmouth Gas DevCo and AEP Ohio Transmission. PJM will study the Flagship Project at the former DOE Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio as one integrated load, generation and transmission package: an initial 800 MW (Mercury, new Monza 345 kV substation, served under the Ohio Power data center tariff) plus about 9,570 MW of additional load (Artemis, new Baku 765 kV substation), for 10,370 MW of firm NITS requested, and about 10,170 MW of gross new GE Vernova gas generation (7HA.2 combined cycle, 6F and aeroderivative units), phased through 2032, with three proposed 765 kV lines. SB Energy's development affiliate pays all study costs ($500,000 deposit, actual cost reimbursed); load flow and short circuit studies are expected within 60 days and stability within 120 days of data review. The filing names OpenAI as the data center tenant, alongside $40 million of SB Energy community benefits and $40 million from OpenAI. Acceptance would not approve any line, cost allocation or interconnection right; PUCO must sign an SAA agreement or issue a binding cost order within 120 days of PJM's final System Upgrade Report or the agreement terminates. Country conversion: a roughly 10 GW US AI campus now has a formal, developer-funded grid study path inside PJM, outside the normal interconnection queue. [Signal 82, Confirmed, via PJM FERC filing ER27-126-000 (13 Oct 2026, primary); Utility Dive 14 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Mason County, Kentucky approves a community benefits agreement with Meta for a hyperscale data center on more than 2,000 zoned acres
item.description: On 13 October 2026 the Mason County Fiscal Court (Maysville, Kentucky) voted unanimously to approve a resolution and community benefits agreement for a hyperscale data center, and Judge-Executive Owen McNeill named Meta as the developer. More than 2,000 acres have been zoned for the project. Reported figures differ: county attorney Jim Parsons put the initial investment at about $15 billion (WKYT), while the agreement as reported by the Ledger Independent and Mason County Post commits $10 billion of capital investment, with about $800 billion of Industrial Revenue Bonds associated with a 40-year, multi-phase plan (about $10 billion per phase). Other terms include more than 2,000 construction jobs, at least 400 full-time jobs, about $115 million of road, water and sewer improvements, and a $15 million public safety fee. Construction of the first phase is expected within three years. Meta's statement calls it a potential project and says it will pay the full cost of the power it uses. No MW, utility or energization date is disclosed. Country conversion: a named hyperscaler secures local approval for a multi-phase Kentucky campus. [Signal 72, Corroborated, via WKYT 13 Oct 2026; Mason County Post 13 Oct (citing Ledger Independent) with Meta statement] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: NeoAI Cloud closes KRW 600 billion of financing for a 40 MW AI data center in Pohang, South Korea, with NHN Cloud pre-leasing half the IT load
item.description: On 12 October 2026 NeoAI Cloud said it completed KRW 600 billion of financing for phase 1 of its Pohang AI data center in the Gwangmyeong industrial complex, North Gyeongsang Province: a KRW 450 billion project finance loan closed on 7 October and KRW 150 billion of equity. NeoAI Cloud and Singapore-based SC Capital Partners are the core equity investors, joined by North Gyeongsang Province, the government Regional Revitalization Investment Fund (its ninth project) and domestic lenders. Phase 1 is 40 MW of utility supply and 32 MW of IT load with liquid cooling for dense GPU clusters; power and the building permit are secured, Hyundai Engineering and Construction has been building since June 2026, and service launch is targeted for Q4 2027. NHN Cloud has committed to pre-lease 16 MW, half the IT capacity. A 260 MW phase 2 is in development. Country conversion: a financed, half-leased AI shell outside the Seoul metro, backed by public regional funds. [Signal 68, Corroborated, via Asia Business Daily 12 Oct 2026; ETNews 12 Oct 2026 (company release)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Bitdeer AI locks an 8-year, 60 MW A103 AI Cloud facility at its Cyberjaya, Malaysia campus
item.description: On 12 October 2026 Bitdeer AI (Bitdeer Technologies Group, NASDAQ: BTDR) announced an 8-year data center services agreement for A103, a 60 MW (critical IT load) AI Cloud facility on the same Cyberjaya, Malaysia campus as A101 and A102. A103 is designed for liquid-cooled, rack-scale NVIDIA systems including the next-generation Vera Rubin platform, with energization expected in Q1 2028. With A103, the Cyberjaya campus is expected to reach about 71.5 MW, and Bitdeer AI's secured AI Cloud capacity (owned or under an executed DCA) rises to about 333.5 MW across Malaysia, Norway and the United States, or about 95% of its up-to-350 MW target for delivery by Q1 2028. An earlier 8 Oct GlobeNewswire version of the same headline was withdrawn the same day (notice to disregard). The company discloses no offtake commitments for A103 capacity as of the release. Country conversion: Malaysia gains another executed 60 MW AI Cloud shell on an existing campus that already has power, liquid cooling and network in place. [Signal 72, Confirmed, via Bitdeer / GlobeNewswire 12 Oct (Markets Insider syndication); Seeking Alpha 12 Oct; Oct 8 disregard notice on GlobeNewswire] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: FERC accepts PJM's 50 MW Large Load definition and registry, rejects the interim curtailment service for new large loads
item.description: On 9 October 2026 FERC issued its order in Docket ER26-3515 (197 FERC 61,019) accepting PJM Interconnection's definition of a Large Load, end-use load with a cumulative peak of 50 MW or more at a single electrical site (affiliated facilities within a one-mile radius count as one site), and a Large Load Registry under which load-serving entities report each large load's location, peak, ramp schedule and backup generation, effective 12 October 2026. FERC rejected the rest of PJM's 13 August filing as one package: the Interim Resource Adequacy Service that could have curtailed new large loads lacking new capacity in emergencies, the Bring Your Own New Capacity rules, and the plan to drop uncovered new large load from the capacity demand curve from the 2029/2030 delivery year. FERC said parts of the tariff appeared to intrude on retail rate regulation. PJM must make a compliance filing within 30 days; Commissioner Rosner concurred separately. No megawatt is added: PJM says its 2028/2029 auction cleared about 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement. Country conversion: the largest US grid now tracks every 50 MW data center site, but new AI load will not face mandatory early curtailment for now. [Signal 86, Confirmed, via FERC eLibrary accession 20261009-3055 (Order, ER26-3515-000); Headwaters Wire 9 Oct; The Duck Curve 10 Oct] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Sesterce plans a EUR 10bn-plus AI campus at the former Kaipola paper mill in Jamsa, Finland: 200 MW first phase, 600 MW second, anchor customer signed
item.description: On 8 October 2026 French AI infrastructure company Sesterce announced a planned investment of over EUR 10 billion in a Sesterce Campus at the former Kaipola paper mill in Jamsa, Central Finland. The first phase, with works planned to start in 2026, is 200 MW, rising to 600 MW in a second phase; Sesterce aims for more than 1 GW of AI capacity in Finland over time. Sesterce says it already has an anchor customer; its CEO told Yle the investment decision is made and a contract is signed with one of the two leading AI labs, without naming it or the financial backers. Grid operator Elenia says the site's high-voltage connection is a solid foundation for the first phase. Sesterce does not yet own the site (seller Kaipola Green Port says talks are advanced), and Jamsa notes permits are still outstanding. Country conversion: a second large AI campus with a signed frontier-lab anchor lands in Finland in the same week as Applied Digital's Finnish power access. [Signal 76, Confirmed, via Sesterce newsroom 8 Oct; Yle News 8 Oct (CEO confirmation of signed client); City of Jamsa release] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Indiana regulators approve AES Indiana's large-load plan to serve Google's 390 MW Monrovia data center
item.description: On 7 October 2026 the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission unanimously approved AES Indiana's large-load growth plan supporting Google's data center in Morgan County (Monrovia), the first data center filed under Indiana's 2025 large-load law (HEA 1007). The project includes solar, two battery storage systems and lines to serve a 390 MW Google facility; WFYI reports total project cost of $737.3 million and AES's estimated infrastructure investment of $1.3 billion. AES says Google's rates cover 100% of energy, infrastructure, transmission and generation costs, with an 80% minimum demand obligation and a contract of at least 15 years; the order still lets $73.8 million of network upgrades go into transmission rate base, which the Citizens Action Coalition opposed. AES estimates about $770 million in customer savings. Country conversion: a state commission converts a 390 MW hyperscale load into an approved, ratepayer-ring-fenced utility build in MISO. [Signal 80, Confirmed, via AES Indiana release 7 Oct; WFYI 12 Oct; Indianapolis Business Journal] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: CoreWeave enters India as sole tenant of a 240 MW AdaniConneX campus in Navi Mumbai, with Vera Rubin planned
item.description: On 7 October 2026 CoreWeave (Nasdaq: CRWV) announced its entry into India through a collaboration with AdaniConneX, the 50:50 Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX joint venture. CoreWeave plans to take 240 MW of data center capacity across three 80 MW buildings at AdaniConneX's Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai as sole tenant, with an option to expand by up to another 240 MW at the campus. It plans to deploy the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, with direct liquid cooling and a non-evaporative chilled water system. The first phase is expected to be available in mid-2028, with more capacity in phases. CoreWeave also plans an India office and local hiring. The release uses plan language, gives no investment figure and names no end customer. Country conversion: a top US neocloud commits to its first Indian campus at hyperscale size. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via CoreWeave release via Business Wire; NDTV Profit; The Next Web] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Applied Digital secures access to up to 1 GW of potential power in Finland for its first non-US AI Factory campus
item.description: On 6 October 2026 Applied Digital (Nasdaq: APLD) said it entered an agreement giving it access to up to 1 GW of potential power capacity in Finland, its first development opportunity outside the United States. The company plans a large-scale AI Factory campus that could scale to as much as 1 GW, with initial power availability anticipated beginning in 2028. It has begun marketing the site and says it is in discussions with leading global hyperscale customers. The release does not name the counterparty, exact site, utility, financing, construction schedule, or a committed tenant. Near-term execution remains centered on the US portfolio. Country conversion: a US AI-campus developer locks Nordic power access for a first international build. [Signal 74, Confirmed, via Applied Digital IR via GlobeNewswire; Yahoo Finance; Grid and Silicon] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: DarkHorse signs up to 50 MW with Hopkinsville Electric System for a new Kentucky superintelligence factory
item.description: On 6 October 2026 DarkHorse Technologies (Nasdaq: DRK) said its subsidiary Pennyrile Holdings signed a power contract with the Electric Plant Board of Hopkinsville, Kentucky (Hopkinsville Electric System) for up to 50 MW for a new superintelligence factory, doubling DarkHorse contracted power in the TVA region to about 100 MW. DarkHorse will fund in full a new 65 MW HES-owned substation on TVA 161 kV, taking 50 MW; about 15 MW is for existing HES customers. The power contract has a ten-year initial term from commencement with automatic five-year renewals. Service remains subject to an eighteen-month permit contingency, utility construction, and other conditions; TVA has approved capacity to serve the project. No end customer is named. Country conversion: contracted municipal utility power for a new US AI campus in Kentucky. [Signal 70, Confirmed, via DarkHorse release via Newsfile; Nasdaq syndication; Christian County Now] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Black Hills signs definitive agreements through 2048 to serve Google's planned Cheyenne, Wyoming data center with a 2.7 GW resource mix
item.description: On 6 October 2026 Black Hills Corp. (NYSE: BKH) said it signed definitive agreements, effective 30 September 2026 with terms through 2048, to serve a planned Google data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming. The project is to be served by a total resource mix of 2.7 GW including reserve margins: up to 590 MW of grid-connected service, mostly from 564 MW of new company-owned natural gas generation at the Cheyenne Prairie Generating Station ($1.8 billion, built 2027 to 2029), plus about 2.1 GW of Wyoming-based third-party contracted resources managed through a private microgrid. Energy service is planned to start in late 2027 and ramp to peak load in 2030. Google has advanced $399 million, refundable, for long-lead equipment and bears all costs of serving the site under the agreements. Transmission filings are still pending at the Wyoming PSC, and the Google campus itself is described as planned. Country conversion: a hyperscaler locks in dedicated multi-GW power for a new US campus. [Signal 86, Confirmed, via Black Hills Corp. release via GlobeNewswire; Form 8-K] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Google signs 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new nuclear uprate capacity plus a 15-year, 2,700 MW supply deal with Constellation in PJM
item.description: On 6 October 2026 Google and Constellation Energy announced a 20-year power purchase agreement that funds uprates at 11 Constellation nuclear units in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, adding 890 MW of new capacity to the PJM grid, with the first uprate expected by 2028 and more than $4.3 billion of Constellation investment. The companies also signed a 15-year energy supply agreement for a further 2,700 MW from Constellation's PJM fleet, about 3,590 MW in total per CNBC. The release frames the deal as a response to PJM's Bring Your Own Power proposal and includes demand-response and load-shaping terms. Power stays on the PJM grid; the release does not name which Google data centers it serves. Country conversion: a hyperscaler pre-funds new firm generation for its PJM load rather than waiting on new interconnection. [Signal 86, Confirmed, via Constellation Energy and Google joint release; CNBC] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: TeraWulf doubles contracted power at its Muskie campus in eastern Kentucky to 1 GW and pulls the second 500 MW into 2029
item.description: On 5 October 2026 TeraWulf (Nasdaq: WULF) said it executed an amended and restated electric service agreement with Kentucky Power, an AEP company, raising contracted capacity at its Muskie Data Campus in eastern Kentucky from 500 MW to 1 GW. The second 500 MW phase moves from 2030 to 2029, subject to Kentucky Public Service Commission approval and Kentucky Power's construction schedule; the first 500 MW phase still targets a 2028 ramp. Kentucky Power is building a 765 kV / 345 kV substation for the site and says the agreement carries about $100 million in customer benefits. TeraWulf says it may take the campus toward 2 GW over time. No tenant is named for Muskie. Country conversion: a US AI campus doubles its contracted utility power ahead of a signed tenant. [Signal 78, Confirmed, via TeraWulf release via GlobeNewswire; Form 8-K; Kentucky Power release; ENR] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: AM Intelligence places firm orders for 20,000 more NVIDIA Rubin GPUs for India and Malaysia (~70 MW, Q2 2027)
item.description: On 5 October 2026 AM Intelligence (AMI), the AI infrastructure platform set up by Greenko's promoters, announced two further firm and binding orders for 20,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, to be deployed as Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems across Malaysia and India, totalling about 70 MW with delivery scheduled for Q2 2027. With the 25 August order for 9,000 Rubin GPUs at its first Hyderabad AI factory, AMI's committed total is about 29,000 Rubin GPUs and close to 100 MW. AMI says it plans to bring a further 300 MW to market over the next 15 months with capex of more than $20 billion, on top of $6 billion already committed for the initial ~100 MW; NVIDIA's Asia South managing director is quoted in the statement. The split of the 70 MW between India and Malaysia and the site locations are not disclosed. Company statement carried by tele.net, BusinessLine and Times of India; no separate NVIDIA release found. [Signal 80, Single-source, via AM Intelligence statement via tele.net; The Hindu BusinessLine] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Applied Digital brings another 75 MW online at Polaris Forge 1 in North Dakota, taking the campus to 250 MW operational
item.description: On 2 October 2026 Applied Digital (Nasdaq: APLD) said it reached Ready for Service on the second phase of Building 2 at its Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota, delivering 75 MW of critical IT load across three 25 MW data halls. That completes Building 2 at 150 MW and brings fully operational critical IT at the campus to 250 MW, against 400 MW contracted at full buildout. The release says the campus is fully leased but does not name the tenant in this announcement; trade press (The Latent) describes it as CoreWeave-leased. Country conversion: contracted US AI capacity becomes energized, usable capacity. [Signal 78, Confirmed, via Applied Digital release via GlobeNewswire] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: JERA, Dell and RHAELM sign MoU for national-scale AI infrastructure in Japan, starting with a 400 MW behind-the-meter campus at Chiba
item.description: On 1 October 2026 JERA, Japan's largest power generator, Dell Technologies and London-based RHAELM signed a memorandum of understanding to build a standardized model for AI infrastructure in Japan. The first project is at JERA's Chiba Thermal Power Station, supported by up to 400 MW of behind-the-meter power, with total capital deployment expected to exceed US$15 billion (2.3 trillion yen) across land, power, construction and AI compute, and operations targeted around 2028. Apollo intends to serve as RHAELM's strategic investment and financing partner, and Dell supplies the rack-scale compute standard. JERA and RHAELM plan to explore more JERA sites toward multi-gigawatt capacity in the 2030s. This is an MoU, not a final investment decision, and no offtake customer is named. Country conversion: Japan's dominant generator commits an operating plant site and power to a named AI campus. [Signal 72, Confirmed, via JERA press release; RHAELM release; Data Center Dynamics] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Nebius signs binding 12-year deal for 50 MW critical IT at AIB Data Centers' southeastern US site
item.description: On 30 September 2026 AIB Data Centers (NYSE American: AIB) announced that a wholly owned subsidiary entered a binding Master Colocation Services Agreement with Nebius (Nasdaq: NBIS) for 50 MW of critical IT capacity at AIB's facility in the southeastern United States, with an initial 12-year term and optional renewals; the release was furnished on Form 8-K. AIB expects Nebius prepayments under the initial term, plus project-level debt and preferred equity, to fund a substantial portion of initial development cost. Capacity is backed by AIB's previously announced 15-year Electric Service Agreement for 65 MW of utility load requiring no significant additional electrical upgrades, and will be delivered in two data halls. The state and contract value are not disclosed in the release; trade press (Baxtel, 2 Oct) reports the first hall within about 10 months and the second within about 14 months, not stated in the primary. Country conversion: a named neocloud tenant converts powered US capacity into long-term contracted MW with customer prepayment financing. [Signal 84, Confirmed, via AIB Data Centers via GlobeNewswire; Form 8-K] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Bitdeer AI contracts >70% offtake on 21.7 MW Johor A201 ahead of Q1 2027 energization
item.description: On 29 September 2026 Bitdeer AI (Bitdeer Technologies Group, Nasdaq: BTDR) announced off-take commitments covering more than 70% of approximately 21.7 MW at its A201 liquid-cooled AI Cloud facility in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, ahead of planned energization in Q1 2027. Expected five-year site revenue exceeds $1.7 billion; company AI Cloud revenue backlog is stated at about $2.9 billion. A201 is purpose-built for NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 with a portion of racks designed for Vera Rubin; Bitdeer says it procured more than 100 GB300 NVL72 racks from an unaffiliated supplier. Together with A202, the Johor campus path is 86.8 MW toward a company target of up to 350 MW AI Cloud capacity by Q1 2028. Customer names are not disclosed. Country conversion: Malaysia gains a named MW AI Cloud campus with majority contracted offtake before energization (distinct from the prior Firmus/OpenAI Malaysia factory Wire). [Signal 82, Single-source, via Bitdeer Technologies Group via GlobeNewswire] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Applied Digital names Brookwood, Alabama as Delta Forge 2 site for 210 MW leased AI campus
item.description: On 24 September 2026 Applied Digital confirmed that Delta Forge 2 — previously disclosed only as a 'new southern state' campus in its 8 June 2026 IR lease release — will be built in Brookwood, Tuscaloosa County, Alabama (~1.26 million sq ft on about 160 acres of a nearly 1,300-acre site). The campus carries the existing 210 MW critical-IT 15-year take-or-pay lease with an unnamed U.S. investment-grade hyperscaler (~$5.2B base-term contracted revenue per the June IR). Combined company-plus-tenant investment is stated above $3.2 billion (TCEDA/TCIDA fact sheet ~$3.2865B). The Tuscaloosa County Economic Development Authority unanimously approved an incentive package of roughly $314.5 million in tax abatements plus $270 million in community-benefit payments over 20 years. Construction is scheduled to begin about 1 October 2026 with completion targeted by end-2028; tenant identity and final County Commission / Brookwood City Council incentive votes remain open. Country conversion: USA Alabama geography unlock plus local incentive package for a named 210 MW AI Factory campus that had no public state/site before 24 Sep. [Signal 84, Corroborated, via WBRC / ABC 33/40 / Tuscaloosa Thread (quoting Applied Digital + TCEDA); lease MW from Applied Digital IR 8 Jun 2026] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: BDx breaks ground on 640 MW CGK4 AI campus in West Java with 845 MVA PLN power
item.description: On 22 September 2026 BDx Data Centers announced groundbreaking on AI Campus 2 (CGK4) in Jatiluhur, West Java, Indonesia: a planned 640 MW AI data-center campus backed by 845 MVA of grid capacity from PLN (part of BDx's stated 1.2 GVA+ secured Indonesia AI-campus power position). Construction has begun on Building 1 of six planned buildings; Building 1 is designed for 120 MW IT capacity in phases, with the first contracted phase expected to enter service in early 2027, using direct-to-chip liquid cooling rated up to 500 kW per rack. West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi and Purwakarta Regent Saepul Bahri Binzein attended. Country conversion: Indonesia adds a named, power-backed AI campus groundbreak with a near-term first-building service window — no named hyperscaler tenant disclosed in the company release. [Signal 90, Confirmed, via BDx Data Centers via PR Newswire] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: New Era (NUAI) TCDC PowerCo signs 20-year 200–207 MW PPA with Vistra/Luminant for Odessa Phase 1
item.description: On 18 September 2026 (8-K filed 21 Sep) TCDC PowerCo LLC, a New Era Energy & Digital subsidiary, entered a Power Purchase Agreement with Luminant ET Services (Vistra affiliate) for a minimum 200 MW and up to 207 MW of energy for Phase 1 of the Texas Critical Data Center near Odessa. Supply is primarily from Vistra's adjacent 1,180 MW Odessa gas plant (or other sources/ERCOT). Initial term 20 years from first Delivery Date; press says contracted power expected available Q3 2027. Credit support: $116M letter of credit within 15 business days of PPA date plus additional security not to exceed $82.8M by Delivery Date (~$198.8M ceiling). Concurrent DFA grants Vistra ROFR on future onsite generation and 5% non-voting Project Company equity once power flows. Campus: 493-acre Permian site with pathway cited to ~1.4 GW; construction permits claimed in Ex.99.1; no named tenant in the September announcement. Country conversion: Permian Phase 1 power is now under a filed 20-year PPA with posted security schedule — Energy/Build for USA, still pre-tenant and pre-delivery. [Signal 91, Confirmed, via New Era Energy & Digital Form 8-K (filed 21 Sep 2026; event 18 Sep) + Ex.99.1] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Kodiak Gas Services contracts 76 MW behind-the-meter baseload to West Texas data center (6-year)
item.description: On 21 September 2026 Kodiak Gas Services (NYSE: KGS) announced a six-year agreement to provide 76 MW of behind-the-meter baseload power capacity, including balance of plant, to a West Texas data center. Deployment: ~40 reciprocating natural-gas generation units beginning Q4 2026 and scaling into Q1 2027, with revenue recognition expected to start Q1 2027. Counterparty described only as a data-center operator contracted with an investment-grade-rated hyperscaler, with a GPU designer as guarantor of the data-center lease — names not disclosed. Kodiak calls this its second long-term primary-power data-center contract; about half of its current power portfolio is now under long-term power contracts. Country conversion: 76 MW BTM gas generation contracted for a hyperscaler-backed West Texas campus with a near-term deploy window — Energy/Build for USA without a named tenant or campus MW beyond the power block. [Signal 86, Confirmed, via Kodiak Gas Services IR press release (21 Sep 2026)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Abbott directs TCEQ to halt all Texas data-center permits pending ERCOT/TWDB audits
item.description: On 21 September 2026 Governor Greg Abbott directed Texas Commission on Environmental Quality Executive Director Kelly Keel to pause issuance of all permits related to data-center projects until ERCOT completes its Large Load review (with TWDB water-use work in parallel). The letter states no other state agency should move forward with data-center regulatory approvals until PUC/ERCOT/TWDB audit information is acquired, and requires TCEQ to update the Governor's office on compliance by Monday 19 October 2026. Country conversion: Texas extends the August interconnect freeze into statewide environmental permitting, widening the stall on AI campus build timelines beyond ERCOT queue gating alone. [Signal 93, Confirmed, via Office of the Governor of Texas (letter PDF)] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: Fluidstack says construction begun on $4B / up to 1.5 GW Cameron County first phase
item.description: On 21 September 2026 Fluidstack published that it has begun construction on the $4 billion first phase of an AI data-center campus in Cameron County, Texas, planned to support up to 1.5 GW of capacity, with more than 2,500 expected construction jobs. Cameron County earlier (10 Sep) issued a worksite permit for site preparation near Valley International Airport; the county notice says future permits are still required before building construction. Fluidstack says it requested no local tax abatement, will pay for energy/infrastructure/water, and will participate in PUCT/ERCOT audits under Abbott directives. item.title: PUCT adopts 16 TAC §25.194 large-load interconnection rule ($50k/MW security; ≥75 MW)
item.description: On 18 September 2026 the Public Utility Commission of Texas filed Order Adopting new 16 TAC §25.194 (Interchange Project 58481 item 218), implementing PURA §37.0561 / SB 6 Large Load Interconnection Standards for ERCOT. Before inclusion in an ERCOT interconnection study, a large-load customer must execute an intermediate agreement, disclose, and post financial security of $50,000 per MW of requested peak demand; a Standard Large Load Interconnection Agreement (SLLIA), further security, and CIAC follow after study. The rule covers customers at or above the 75 MW large-load threshold. Same-day item 219 is the Texas Register Acknowledgement of Receipt (TRD 202604027) for the 10/02/2026 issue; Interchange describes effectiveness as of 10.08.2026. Country conversion: Texas’s permanent ≥75 MW interconnect rule is now stamped — Batch Zero and subsequent large-load queues run under a live security and disclosure regime rather than staff draft. [Signal 92, Confirmed, via PUCT Interchange 58481 item 218 Order Adopting; item 219 Texas Register ack] More: https://compute.world/wire.html

item.title: PUCT files written Order on Howard–Solstice 765 kV (59336) — Route 4 mod 1 CCN
item.description: On 18 September 2026 PUCT OPDM filed the written Order in Docket 59336 (Interchange item 2741), amending AEP Texas CCN 30028 and CPS Energy CCN 30031 to build and operate the Howard-to-Solstice ~370-mile 765 kV single-circuit line along Route 4 mod 1 (not SOAH’s recommended Route 4). The Order cites lower estimated cost/length vs Route 4, ~60.3 miles (16.53%) paralleling existing ROW, and an estimated line cost of $2.15 billion for Route 4 mod 1; authority runs seven years unless energized sooner. This stamps the 11 Sep open-meeting approval that prior Wire tracked as pending written order. item.title: CleanSpark prices $2.276B 7.875% senior notes (upsized) to finish Meta-anchored Sandersville AI campus
item.description: On 18 September 2026 CleanSpark filed an 8-K with Exhibit 99.1 stating subsidiary CSDC Finance I, LLC priced a $2.276 billion offering of 7.875% senior secured notes due 2031 at 98.500% of principal (upsized from the 17 Sep proposed $2.227B).
